# Empty and Split Commits

After this page you can create a commit that records no tree change with `--allow-empty`, recognize why a second empty commit fails without that flag, and split a lumped commit into focused commits with a mixed reset.

## Thesis

Most commits exist to record a new tree. Two exceptions come up constantly in real work. First, you sometimes want a **commit that changes no files** — a marker for a deploy hook, a CI no-op, or a merge-base you can point at — and Git will refuse that unless you pass `--allow-empty`. Second, you sometimes record **too much in one commit** and need to split it before you share the branch.

Both are local history edits. The empty-commit flag is safe to use on a branch you will push. Splitting already-pushed commits is a rewrite; do it on a topic branch that has not been shared, or be prepared to coordinate a force-push.

Verified with **git 2.47.3**.

## Mental model

```text
  git commit                  requires a change in the index vs HEAD
  git commit --allow-empty    records a new commit with the same tree as HEAD

  split a lumped commit:
    HEAD  = WIP that touches a.txt and b.txt
    git reset HEAD~1          moves HEAD back, leaves the work in the tree
    git add a.txt && commit
    git add b.txt && commit
```

A mixed reset (`git reset HEAD~1`, the default mode) keeps the file contents and unstages them. Soft would keep the index staged; hard would throw the work away. The lab used mixed.

## Lab

```text
[main (root-commit) b826c92] add a and b together
 2 files changed, 2 insertions(+)
 create mode 100644 a.txt
 create mode 100644 b.txt
===== allow empty =====
[main 7f1a4ef] chore: marker for a deploy hook
7f1a4ef chore: marker for a deploy hook
b826c92 add a and b together
===== empty without flag fails =====
On branch main
nothing to commit, working tree clean
empty_commit_exit=1
===== split a lumped commit =====
Switched to a new branch 'split-demo'
[split-demo cd15540] WIP: change a and b in one lump
 2 files changed, 2 insertions(+)
Unstaged changes after reset:
M	a.txt
M	b.txt
===== after mixed reset =====
 M a.txt
 M b.txt
[split-demo 100072d] update a only
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)
[split-demo 0ca4a4c] update b only
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)
0ca4a4c (HEAD -> split-demo) update b only
100072d update a only
7f1a4ef (main) chore: marker for a deploy hook
b826c92 add a and b together
```

The empty commit `7f1a4ef` has the same tree as `b826c92`; only the commit object (message, parent, author) is new. Repeating `git commit -m 'should fail'` with a clean tree exited `1` and printed `nothing to commit, working tree clean`.

The split was done on `split-demo`, not by rewriting `main`. `git reset HEAD~1` dropped `cd15540` from the branch tip (it remains reachable from the reflog until expiry) and left both files modified in the worktree. Staging and committing them separately produced `100072d` and `0ca4a4c`.

Interactive rebase can also split a commit (`edit` that commit, reset, and recommit). That path was not run here.

## Pitfalls

1. Forgetting `--allow-empty` and reading "nothing to commit" as a repository problem. The tree really is unchanged.
2. Using `git reset --hard` when you meant to split — that discards the lumped work.
3. Splitting a commit that is already on a shared branch without coordinating a rewrite.
4. Stopping after `git reset` and accidentally committing both files together again. Check `git status` and add paths one at a time.

## Worked scenarios

### Scenario A — a deploy hook that looks for a new SHA

Some deployment systems fire on a new commit on a branch even when the tree is identical. `git commit --allow-empty -m 'chore: retrigger deploy'` produces that SHA. The lab's `7f1a4ef` is that shape.

### Scenario B — a "WIP" commit that mixed two fixes

Branch off, reset the lumped tip, and remake the commits as in the lab. Confirm with `git log --oneline` that each resulting commit touches one concern (`update a only`, `update b only`).

### Scenario C — you already pushed the lumped commit

Do not reset shared `main`. Either add follow-up commits, or split on a replacement topic branch and force-push only that branch after the team agrees. This lab did not force-push.

## Summary

- `--allow-empty` records a commit with no tree change; without it, Git exits 1 on a clean tree.
- A mixed `git reset HEAD~1` is a practical way to split the latest commit on a private branch.
- Split on a topic branch; treat already-pushed history as public.
- The empty marker commit and the split commits in this lab are `7f1a4ef`, `100072d`, and `0ca4a4c`.
